Photocatalysis offers a green route to uranium recovery, but its practical deployment is hindered by rapid charge recombination and reliance on sacrificial agents or external bias. Here, we introduce an osmotic-energy-coupled photoelectrochemical platform that directly converts a natural salinity gradient into a driving force for charge separation, enabling reagent-free uranium (VI) reduction from seawater. The designed heterostructure combines a p-type hole transport layer with uranyl-selective nano-pockets, and its integration with a cation-selective membrane allows the harvested osmotic energy to suppress electron–hole recombination. This coupling boosted uranium extraction efficiency by over 400% at natural seawater concentrations, demonstrating strong applicability in ultra-trace environments. This work offers a sustainable pathway for metal recovery from dilute and complex aqueous systems. An osmotic-energy-coupled photoelectrochemical system is developed for enhanced uranium extraction from seawater. A salinity gradient across a cation-selective membrane generates spontaneous electron flow, promoting charge separation and suppressing electron–hole recombination in the NiO@UiO-66-3C4N photocathode. This coupling enhances U(VI) photoreduction without sacrificial agents or external bias, increasing uranium extraction efficiency by over 400% at natural seawater concentrations. The strategy provides a sustainable approach to utilizing naturally available salinity-gradient energy for uranium recovery.

title: Stabilizing SrVO₃ bottom electrodes for high-k SrTiO₃ integration via La-doped STO passivation and O₃-reduced atomic layer deposition
abstract: Abstract The increasing demand for higher capacitance density in dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) has driven the need to integrate high- k dielectric materials. SrTiO 3 (STO) has emerged as a promising candidate owing to its high dielectric constant of over 100 in thin-film form. To achieve a high dielectric constant for STO, it is crucial to select bottom electrode materials with superior lattice matching with STO. This study evaluates the potential of SrVO 3 (SVO) electrodes used with atomic layer deposition (ALD) STO, thereby addressing the challenges associated with the stability of SVO during the ALD STO process. The results indicate that applying La:STO oxygen-blocking layers effectively mitigates SVO degradation during the ALD process. Furthermore, reducing the O 3 concentration during ALD enabled the successful integration of high-quality STO on SVO with a bulk dielectric constant of 175 and exceptionally well-maintained interfacial properties. This study evaluates SVO as a promising electrode candidate for utilizing STO in next-generation DRAM and demonstrates its potential to provide increased capacitance density and reduced leakage currents.

title: A flexible tissue-adhesive nanocomposite hydrogel for Wi-Fi-enabled electro-responsive drug release and biomonitoring
abstract: Mechanically adaptive, conductive, and tissue-adhesive hydrogels integrated with wireless bioelectronics offer a promising platform for wearable therapeutics and real-time biomonitoring. Most existing platforms address these functions separately, lacking a single integrated platform capable of both real-time sensing and wirelessly controlled on-demand drug delivery. Herein, a multifunctional conductive hydrogel has been designed to enable real-time motion sensing and on-demand electro-triggered drug release in an open-loop system controlled via Wi-Fi. To achieve this, a simple free radical polymerization (FRP) method has been adopted to synthesize a nanocomposite hydrogel, designated CycloStik-Q, composed of β-cyclodextrin (β-CD), N-hydroxymethylacrylamide (NHMA), and graphene quantum dots (GQDs) derived from cigarette smoke extract. This synthetic strategy yields a composite hydrogel that exhibits a distinctive combination of properties, including remarkable stretchability and flexibility, stab resistance, electro-responsiveness, pressure sensitivity, high optical transparency, antioxidant activity, and effective UV-blocking performance. These integrated characteristics have been leveraged to fabricate a flexible, wireless sensor platform capable of real-time human motion tracking via Wi- Fi-enabled communication, highlighting its potential for remote and at-home monitoring. Additionally, the hydrogel functions as an on-demand electro-responsive drug delivery system with wirelessly controlled, user-triggered release, underscoring its potential for personalized therapeutic applications. The integration of soft materials with wireless electronics is revolutionizing wearable healthcare, enabling continuous physiological monitoring and therapeutic responses. This study introduces CycloStik-Q, a nanocomposite hydrogel that combines real-time biomechanical motion sensing with wirelessly controlled drug release, addressing limitations of traditional biomonitoring methods. Researchers synthesized graphene quantum dots (GQDs) from cigarette smoke extract and integrated them into a hydrogel matrix composed of β-cyclodextrin, N-hydroxymethylacrylamide, with enhanced conductivity and mechanical properties. CycloStik-Q exhibits robust stretchability, strong tissue adhesion, and excellent conductivity, suitable for long-term skin integration. It enables remote monitoring of physiological signals like joint motion, cardiac activity, along with Wi-Fi-controlled drug release. This dual functionality distinguishes CycloStik-Q from conventional sensors, offering a sustainable, multifunctional platform for next-generation wearable healthcare systems. Future directions include personalized diagnostics and therapy in remote or resource-limited settings, enhancing patient care. This summary was initially drafted using artificial intelligence, then revised and fact-checked by the author.

title: Non-toxic aryl diazirine photoinitiators
abstract: Photoinitiators offer an energy-saving alternative to thermal initiation, initiating free-radical polymerization through irradiation. Despite their benefits, current photoinitiators face issues of toxicity and solubility. Trifluoromethylphenyl diazirine, an aryl diazirine, is a promising photoinitiator that generates a carbene upon exposure to light. Aryl diazirines exhibit favorable optical and molecular properties, including minimal skin sensitization and liquid miscibility with aqueous and organic resins. Experimental studies demonstrate the ability of aryl diazirines to initiate free-radical polymerization of acrylate monomers, offering several advantages over traditional photoinitiators, such as TPO and BAPO. Aryl diazirines’ unique attributes include low cytotoxicity, prevention of resin shrinkage, and removal of unreacted monomers post-curing. R-group variants enable both UV and visible-light activation, thereby expanding their utility across biomedical and industrial sectors. The study explores the potential of aryl diazirines as photoinitiators for acrylate polymerization, addressing the limitations of current photoinitiators like toxicity and solubility. The authors hypothesize that aryl diazirines, with electron-withdrawing or alkyl para-substituents, can initiate radical polymerization effectively. They employ photorheometry to assess the polymerization process under various wavelengths and conditions, comparing results with commercial photoinitiators. The findings reveal that aryl diazirines achieve comparable mechanical properties to TPO, with advantages such as lower skin sensitization and better solubility in water-based resins. These properties make aryl diazirines promising for applications in biomedical fields and sustainable manufacturing. The study suggests future exploration of diazirines in 3D printing and bioadhesives, emphasizing their potential as non-toxic alternatives to traditional photoinitiators. This summary was initially drafted using artificial intelligence, then revised and fact-checked by the author. Aryl diazirines as a new class of photoinitiators. Irradiation of an aryl diazirine releases N2 and generates a triplet carbene that initiates free-radical polymerization of acrylate monomers through a hypothesized hydrogen abstraction mechanism. Unlike commercial photoinitiators, aryl diazirines exhibit unique benefits like being miscible liquids in both organic and aqueous environments, exhibit minimal cytotoxicity, and can absorb residual vinyl monomer through the diazoalkane isomer. The para-substituent tunes activation wavelength from 365 to 445 nm and nitrogen evolution offsets cure shrinkage.

title: From deterministic to adaptive magnetic micro-robots
abstract: Abstract Robotics has long pursued the development of systems that can control physical objects remotely and precisely in diverse environments. With ongoing miniaturization, micro-robots have emerged as promising platforms for a wide range of applications. In particular, magnetic micro-robots are compelling because external magnetic fields provide a wireless and biocompatible means of actuation, overcoming the constraints of on-board power sources in confined and complex settings. Despite extensive studies, the classification of magnetic micro-robots has often remained indistinct. This review seeks to contribute a more systematic understanding by defining four major categories—rigid, reconfigurable, shape-changing, and swarm—while also discussing emerging hybrid systems that bridge these paradigms. We synthesize the fundamental actuation principles and representative designs of each category. By examining the capabilities and limitations of each paradigm, we identify challenges and outline future directions for the advancement of adaptive and intelligent magnetic micro-robotic systems.
